title: Using Neighborhood Data in Aging Research: The National Neighborhood Data Archive (NaNDA). Workshop Materials, GSA Annual Scientific Meeting Online Workshop Series 2026
description:
Materials from the two-hour virtual workshop Using Neighborhood Data in Aging Research: The National Neighborhood Data Archive (NaNDA), presented October 7, 2026 as part of the GSA Annual Scientific Meeting Online Workshop Series 2026.

The National Neighborhood Data Archive (NaNDA) is a federally funded open data repository at the University of Michigan Institute for Social Research that publishes neighborhood-level measures of the social, economic, and built environment through ICPSR. The workshop introduces NaNDA, walks through examples of its use in gerontological research, and offers two parallel breakout tracks: a beginner track on choosing a first NaNDA dataset (geographies, time periods, and dataset selection) and an intermediate track on linking NaNDA measures to participant data.

This record contains the presentation slides for the full-group sessions and the beginner breakout (web page, PowerPoint, and PDF for each), the beginner participant handout, and supporting tools. Speaker notes are not included. The intermediate breakout materials (practice data and sample merge code) are published separately at https://the-national-neighborhood-data-archive.github.io/GSA_Intermediate_2026/.

Presenters: Philippa Clarke, Lindsay Gypin, William Clary, Robert Melendez, and Grace Noppert, University of Michigan.
